envelope.text: where upstream's shares ownership, and it never throws `bad_weak_ptr`

why: upstream gets this from `std::enable_shared_from_this<Node>` and the returned pointer SHARES OWNERSHIP; ours is a method returning `Node::SharedPtr`, which since phase-482 W2 is `nros::Handle<Node>` on every target: it observes `this` without extending the node's lifetime. The base class is what forced the change, not a preference: it carries a `std::weak_ptr` member that exists only where `<memory>` does, so deriving from it would make `sizeof(Node)` follow a capability probe -- the defect `check-cpp-capability-layout` exists to catch (phase-427 W1). In this API a node is constructed by the generated entry or by `main` and outlives everything it is handed to, so the two behave the same; a caller who stores the handle past the node's scope gets a dangling one where upstream would have kept the node alive. Ours also never throws, where upstream raises `bad_weak_ptr` on a node no `shared_ptr` owns (RFC-0018). Before phase-482 W2 this returned a hosted-only aliasing `std::shared_ptr` with an empty owner -- the same observe-only contract, unavailable freestanding.
